newsitem.title: INDIA: Shortage of quality Indian cotton lifts prices.
newsitem.headline: Shortage of quality Indian cotton lifts prices.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Friday gained partly due to a shortage of quality varieties, dealers said.
Fresh mill buying also lifted prices. Arrivals were low.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by five rupees at 890/950 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned moved up by 10 rupees at 1,500/1,640 rupees per maund. F-414 lifted by 5/10 rupees at 1,890/1,910 rupees per maund while Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose by 200 rupees at 12,200/12,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).

"Out of the new crop of 16 million bales (170 kg each) about 12/13 million bales has already been marketed and traders were witnessing easing pressure of arrivals as well as a shortage of good quality cotton," one broker said.
"Blenders remained active buyers in the average quality to mix it up with superior cotton," he added.
